references.text: The regulations concerning the showbread (לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים) in the books of Moses. Only priests were allowed to eat them, which Jesus refers to in his argument.
The account of David entering God's house and eating the showbread that only priests were permitted to eat. This is the Old Testament event Jesus refers to in Luke 6:4.
The instruction to place the showbread (לֶחֶם פָּנִים) on the table before the Lord's face. This is the background for the holy bread that David ate.
The regulation that only Aaron and his sons (the priests) were to eat of the holy bread. Jesus points out that David broke this rule.
Matthew's parallel account where Jesus uses the same argument about David and the showbread to defend the disciples' plucking of grain on the Sabbath.
Mark's parallel account where Jesus refers to David entering God's house and eating the showbread that only priests were allowed to eat.
